units.name: MenuPasswordVramRecords
units.summary: Adjacent terminated VRAM records, password/menu strings and tile text consumed by the inline display helpers. These are multiple records, not one claimed parsed container; unparsed substructure remains generic Data.

units.name: InitializeNewStage_VramPointer
units.summary: Inline little-endian VRAM command pointer. The transfer helper reads these two bytes and advances the saved return past them; execution resumes after the word.

units.name: InitializeNewStage_CallTransferInlineVramCommands_VramPointer
units.summary: Inline little-endian VRAM command pointer. The transfer helper reads these two bytes and advances the saved return past them; execution resumes after the word.

units.name: ResetTailFill
units.summary: Uniform $FF bytes after the reset JMP and before the vector table. Non-code data; original fill purpose is not established.

units.name: AudioEntryVectors
units.summary: Three public JMP entries: select music (A), select an effect (A), and advance audio once. Bank 8 must occupy $8000; music/effect data at $A000 need their matching bank. These are CPU aliases, not permanent ROM identities.

units.name: SelectMusic
units.summary: A selects a two-byte pointer at $8C00. Disable APU channels, copy eight stream-pointer bytes to $C2..C9, reset four note timers, then enable the four tonal/noise channels. Clear effect ownership and initialize cached pulse/noise volume.

units.name: SelectSoundEffect
units.summary: Ignore a new effect while either effect channel owns hardware. Otherwise set ownership bits 7/6 and copy two stream pointers from the effect directory at $B840 into $E8..EB; clear their timers. A is the effect index, doubled for the directory.

units.name: AdvancePulse1Music
units.summary: Pulse 1 is a bytecode stream at ($C2), with a timer in $DA. A note packs pitch in the upper nibble and duration in the lower nibble. Duration is the shared base shifted by bits 0..2, plus half that value when bit 3 is set. Notes fetch a period pair through ($D2). Upper nibbles C..F dispatch controls: envelope/sweep, duration base, absolute stream jump, saved return, stream call, stop/rest, or period-table selection. Stream calls save one return pointer, not a nesting stack. Commit Y to the stream pointer only after processing the event. Envelope bit 4 selects direct volume; otherwise the envelope table supplies a held countdown and volume step.

units.name: AdvancePulse2Music
units.summary: Commit pulse 1 volume and tick its timers, then decode pulse 2 using the same event grammar as pulse 1. Pulse 2 uses $C4/$D4 and $DB. Always update the cached hardware image; suppress live pulse 2 writes when an effect owns it (ownership bit 7). The envelope and duration calculations mirror pulse 1.

units.name: AdvanceTriangleMusic
units.summary: Commit pulse 2 envelope state, then decode triangle events through ($C6). Triangle notes write a period pair through ($D6) and set the length-load bit. Controls share stream jump/call/return and duration semantics, but configure the linear counter instead of a pulse envelope. $DC counts remaining note ticks.

units.name: AdvanceNoiseMusic
units.summary: Decode noise stream ($C8), with duration in $DD. Notes select an envelope position from the upper nibble; control events share the stream flow and duration grammar. Period selection uses the lower nibble directly. Cache noise registers even while an effect owns noise (ownership bit 6); advance the stream after consuming an event.

units.name: CommitNoiseEnvelope
units.summary: Choose fixed or table-stepped noise volume, cache it, and write hardware only when noise is not reserved by an effect. Tick the music noise timer before proceeding to effects.

units.name: AdvancePulseEffect
units.summary: Decode the pulse effect stream ($E8), which temporarily owns pulse 2. This smaller grammar supports envelope/sweep, duration base, stop and period-table selection. Effects have independent duration/envelope state. A stop holds the stream on its stop token and sets bit 7 of the release flags; hardware restoration occurs below when its duration expires.

units.name: CheckNoiseEffectOwnership
units.summary: Only advance the noise effect while ownership bit 6 is set. Otherwise proceed directly to channel restoration.

units.name: AdvanceNoiseEffect
units.summary: Decode noise effects from ($EA), with their own duration base and envelope position. A stop sets release bit 6 and holds the token. The effect writes live noise period and volume; the music register image remains available for restoration.

units.name: ReleasePulseEffect
units.summary: When pulse-effect stop was seen and its timer reaches zero, clear only ownership bit 7 and restore all four pulse 2 registers from the music cache. Preserve noise-effect ownership.

units.name: ReleaseNoiseEffect
units.summary: When noise-effect stop was seen and its timer reaches zero, clear only ownership bit 6 and restore all four noise registers from the cached music image. Preserve pulse-effect ownership.

units.name: FinishAudioTick
units.summary: Return after music/effect updates and any channel restoration.

units.name: EnterAttractScene
units.summary: Request display/audio mode $08 through the interrupt handshake, then initialize the title display resources.

units.name: AttractWaitLoop
units.summary: Wait for a frame, poll controllers and update the random state. On qualifying frame counts, tick the scene counter; Start exits the wait and the timeout selects an attract room.

units.name: AttractGameplayLoop
units.summary: Run falcon, enemy, effect, projectile, sprite and background updates once per frame, then poll input/random state. The countdown returns toward the attract entry; Start moves to menu setup. Demo input provenance belongs to phase-1 scenarios, not a natural player route.

units.name: InitializeMainMenu
units.summary: Clear eight progress/digit bytes, reset demo mode, select music 1, set display mode, load palette and scene graphics, reset objects and scrolling, then draw menu content. Inline pointer words after display helpers are inline data skipped by the transfer helper.

units.name: BuildMenuActors
units.summary: Construct the two menu actor records. Selection bits in $8D choose their positions; field meanings are shared with the game object renderer. Request music $0D and an effect before entering the input loop.

units.name: MenuSelectionInput
units.summary: Update the menu actor and OAM, poll new button edges, and toggle the $40 controller-mode or $20 menu-choice bit in $8D. Restart the presentation after a selection change. These bits are later consumed by player/falcon control and menu dispatch.

units.name: AcceptMenuSelection
units.summary: Start accepts the selection. One branch resets the completed-country mask and progression fields before stage selection; the password path edits and validates ten letters.

units.name: EnterStageSelection
units.summary: Discard the old call stack. Progress value $0F selects the altar scene; otherwise initialize the stage-selection screen.

units.name: InitializeStageSelector
units.summary: Set selection-mode flags and music, load scene/palette and nametable content, build country text, set PRG data bank, and initialize the stage cursor. Stage selection starts at zero; the selection helper skips completed destinations.

units.name: StageSelectorInput
units.summary: Each frame animates the cursor, builds OAM and polls input. A advances through seven destinations, B moves backward, Select calls a separate handler, and Start clears the room index before stage initialization. The selector helper exposes Ruth (index 7) once the seven completion bits are set.

units.name: ChooseAvailableStage
units.summary: A gives search direction. Search the seven country bit masks against completed countries, wrapping in either direction; all seven complete selects stage 7. Store the selected stage and its cursor position, restart animation and queue a selection sound.

units.name: AnimateStageCursor
units.summary: Every fourth frame move the actor horizontally; reverse facing every 32 steps. Advance an animation stream, wrapping on its negative sentinel, then dispatch its selector through the inline table helper. The tail also adjusts vertical position and resets animation fields.

units.name: AnimateMenuActor
units.summary: Select object zero and animation parameters, increment its frame counter, then tail-call the common animation helper. The next small entry invokes an inline VRAM transfer.

units.name: BuildCountryTextRows
units.summary: Build paired VRAM command buffers at $05B0/$0600: address, count $1C, 28 tile bytes and negative terminator. Seven rows advance nametable addresses by $60. A completion bit chooses a country row or the fallback text; source arrays at $AC66/$AD66 provide the upper/lower tile rows.

units.name: EnterStage
units.summary: Reset stack, initialize stage state and status text, then wait/poll before entering the game loop. The alternate entry reinitializes a room while retaining progression state.

units.name: GameplayFrame
units.summary: Poll controllers, update player/falcon/enemies/effects/projectiles, render OAM and update room state, then wait for the next frame. A nonzero transition request exits the frame loop; zero continues.

units.name: HandleRoomTransition
units.summary: Low three request bits choose the next room and retain player state through the room initializer. A request with those bits clear instead changes actor states and enters a separate timed transition sequence that hides the actors before advancing the room.

units.name: ProcessDefeatedObjectEvent
units.summary: When display updates are idle and an object event is pending, index the room event table with event plus room base. Small values queue audio; larger values select a bounded event subtype and a helper according to room group. The bounded inline event table selects decimal score awards before the shared status update.

units.name: BuildStatusDigits
units.summary: Build an eight-character status row from $07E0..E7, suppressing leading zeroes as spaces. Remaining digits become tiles by OR $30. Queue VRAM upload and clear the pending object-event byte.

units.name: TickActorFlashTimers
units.summary: Maintain player/falcon flashing timers: mask facing into the flags, alternate low palette bits with frame phase, then restore their normal palette and immunity timer on expiry. A third timer ticks every fourth frame.

units.name: UpdatePlayerInput
units.summary: Skip input while room control is locked. Process player damage/status first, then choose controller 1 or 2 for falcon commands according to the menu controller-mode bit. An active player recovery timer bypasses ordinary movement.

units.name: DispatchFalconCommands
units.summary: Recognize B plus Up/Down combinations and call release/recall or attack handlers. With separate falcon control enabled, directional input changes falcon facing or target height within bounds; common movement helpers apply the motion.

units.name: DispatchPlayerMotionState
units.summary: Dispatch the player movement state through an inline table. Classified states update attack timers and rising/falling motion, then interpret ordinary held directional input through movement helpers. Inline target words are data selected states are supported by the initialization and explicit state writers.

units.name: PlayerActionEdges
units.summary: Process Start and Select edge handlers, then track sustained horizontal-only input while the player is idle. The purpose of that duration counter is inferred from its movement consumer below, not original variable names.

units.name: ResolvePlayerGroundState
units.summary: When player immunity and movement state permit, probe the lower tile edge. Tile categories choose a falling state and reset its phase; sustained directional input controls the remembered horizontal fall direction.

units.name: CheckPlayerVerticalBoundary
units.summary: Check the player against top/bottom screen bounds, using frame-specific height. Prepare a map probe just outside the body; paired tile samples select a nonreserved motion nibble.

units.name: CheckPlayerLifeAndRecovery
units.summary: Handle a delayed player recovery/death mode, then inspect player health. With no health, stop ordinary motion and hide the sword; otherwise preserve active movement states. A special frame sets recovery sentinel $FF. The omitted continuations remain uncertain.

units.name: TickPlayerRecovery
units.summary: Skip ordinary recovery work while a flashing timer is active. Tick immunity or recovery time and probe the upper edge when needed. The recovery continuation moves upward until blocked and selects the next standing or traversal state.

units.name: ResolvePlayerPlatformContact
units.summary: Scan player/object overlap. A retained platform object aligns player Y above its top and can carry the player sideways according to the platform facing on alternating frames. $7D distinguishes platform contact from ordinary hit targets.

units.name: ApplyPlayerCollisionDamage
units.summary: Use the selected overlap target and sprite category to choose damage behavior. Ignore damage during either participant immunity. Set knockback/recovery animation, hide the sword, choose sound and reduce player health with saturation at zero. The extended death sequence is outside the classified fragments.

units.name: DispatchPlayerRightMotion
units.summary: Use player state 0..2 to select the corresponding grounded directional handler from inline words. Jump and fall states route through their own direction tables.

units.name: StartPlayerJump
units.summary: A new A edge starts rising state 3 with phase zero. The rising handler consumes a phase-indexed motion table; values below $10 are speed steps, while larger values dispatch control actions.

units.name: PlayerPostureTransitions
units.summary: Adjust player Y and base/display frame for crouched/standing postures; retain held horizontal input as jump/fall direction. Independent RTS-delimited entries share this classified fragment.

units.name: AdvancePlayerJump
units.summary: Use the jump-table value as a pixel-step budget. Holding A after the early phase prolongs upward motion. Probe the upper body edge before each decrement of screen Y; obstruction or release enters falling state.

units.name: AdvancePlayerFall
units.summary: Initialize or advance falling state 4. Early phases use the fall table, later phases move four pixels per tick. Probe ground per pixel and stop when tile categories support the actor; preserve horizontal direction through the inline movement dispatch.

units.name: FinishPlayerLanding
units.summary: On landing, align the standing/crouched frame and hold the landing phase near $F4. A can restart rising immediately; after the landing phase, Down chooses crouch, otherwise restore idle standing position and state.

units.name: StartPlayerAttack
units.summary: A new B edge begins sword attack; A with vertical input can begin a secondary attack if its slot is free. Store a 16-tick attack timer and variant, select CHR state, and queue sound. Secondary attack requires sufficient resource and its actual spawn occurs at the midpoint below.

units.name: AnimateSwordAttack
units.summary: Count down the attack. On expiry restore the player frame and hide sword slot $10. Otherwise combine timer and body-frame tables to choose sword/body graphics, copy player Y/facing, and place the sword 16 pixels to the facing side before overlap testing.

units.name: SpawnSecondaryAttack
units.summary: At attack tick 8, require nonzero resource/type and enough resource for the type cost. Deduct cost, construct slot $30 at the player position with cleared state/timers, initialize fixed-point motion, and queue its sound. The selected weapon handler then advances its own motion/state machine in slot $30.

units.name: MovePlayerRight
units.summary: Move right by one pixel after right-edge tile probes and map bounds. Facing is updated by the wrapper. In the entrance room clamp X at $F0; in later rooms compute a two-page camera X centered near $78, clamped at world limits. Leftward helpers use matching world and collision bounds before updating the facing and animation.

units.name: AnimateWalkingPlayer
units.summary: Choose displayed body frame from base frame and animation counter. Idle/walking uses one frame per eight ticks; early movement states use four ticks. Other states preserve their explicit body frame. Weapon selection and projectile handlers follow.

units.name: UpdateProjectileGraphics
units.summary: The first entry cycles a CHR bank from a four-entry frame-phase table. The next entry selects projectile slot $30, checks visibility, and dispatches the selected secondary-attack type. Seven supported weapon types select distinct motion handlers.

units.name: FalconCommandHandlers
units.summary: Release/recall depends on falcon state: inactive initializes its world position and target height from the player; active flight switches between following and free flight. Attack command only changes free-flight state 3 to state 4 and resets its phase.

units.name: UpdateFalcon
units.summary: Hide and deactivate the falcon when its health reaches zero. Otherwise select slot $20, shared animation settings and collision flags; tick its immunity timer and dispatch its state. A second inline dispatch selects a handler by player state.

units.name: PositionPerchedFalcon
units.summary: Put the falcon eight pixels above the player, with a two-pixel horizontal facing offset and a body-frame-dependent one-pixel bob. Copy player facing and preserve falcon palette bit.

units.name: FalconFollowSetup
units.summary: A following state copies the player location and cycles four wing frames. Other entries initialize falcon motion or set approach speeds before comparing its world X against the player.

units.name: MoveFalconTowardPlayer
units.summary: Compare two-byte world X and move in the needed facing direction; compare Y against player Y minus eight and move vertically. Common fixed-point helpers track requested movement bits.

units.name: FinishFalconApproach
units.summary: Select animation timing from the movement-result bits. When the approach reaches the target with no requested movement, return the falcon to perched state zero.

units.name: MoveFalconToFlightHeight
units.summary: Compare falcon Y with its target height. Matching height enters free-flight state 3; otherwise use upward/downward movement and animation, then perform collision checks. The adjacent handlers use bounded motion streams and camera-relative facing checks.

units.name: CheckFalconContact
units.summary: Find a collision target for falcon slot $20. Low sprite categories dispatch special contact; other targets can damage the falcon unless its immunity timer is active.

units.name: CheckSwordContact
units.summary: Select sword slot $10 as the attack origin, clear attack flags and scan targets. A target attribute high bit makes it immune to this sword path; otherwise prepare sword height and damage animation parameters.

units.name: ApplyFalconDamage
units.summary: Respect target and falcon immunity, subtract category damage from falcon health with saturation at zero, start immunity and sound, and force an airborne falcon into return state. Separate contact handlers below apply weapon-specific damage and pickups.

units.name: DispatchAttackedObjectCategory
units.summary: Classify target behavior from the attribute table indexed by object kind. Negative categories choose special interactions, room-persistent events or generic damage. $D0/$E0/$F0 are category markers, not CPU addresses.

units.name: SpecialContactState
units.summary: Store the attack subtype and reject high sprite categories. A short prefix restores a saved object type once its animation age reaches eight; the continuation saturates resource pickups or grants the room weapon ownership bit.

units.name: DispatchRoomPersistentEvent
units.summary: Reject an event already recorded for this room. Otherwise dispatch the low nibble of its category through an inline table. Most event handlers are not classified yet.

units.name: DamageOrdinaryObject
units.summary: Select damage from attack type and room modifiers. A timed modifier can double damage; object immunity prevents repeated hits. Subtract from per-object health and store a pending object event when it reaches zero. No natural reachability is inferred for static-only fragments.

units.name: QueueDefeatedObjectEvent
units.summary: Read the defeated object category, store its event selector, and clear health. The following transition preserves the original kind and initializes pickup or room reward state.

units.name: InitializeHitSpark
units.summary: Start a 16-tick hit spark at the attack origin. Copy two-byte world X and supplied Y; facing shifts the spark eight pixels to the other side.

units.name: RenderHitSpark
units.summary: Tick the spark and convert world X to camera-relative X. If visible on the current page, write one OAM sprite with frame-driven flip; otherwise hide its OAM slot.

units.name: AdvanceRoomTileEvent
units.summary: Start a staged tile event when requested, preserving its timer. Later phases wait before initiating restoration; stage 7 is excluded from that timer path. These event phases are consumed in the interrupt handler.

units.name: BuildRoomEventTileCommands
units.summary: Construct two VRAM commands for adjacent tile columns, with high-bit count selecting vertical increment. Terminate at $FF, queue upload and request the event sound. The nametable address was captured while building the room.

units.name: UpdatePrimaryEnemyController
units.summary: A negative room controller falls through to ordinary object updates. Otherwise dispatch boss/special-room state when active; if its primary object health is zero, enter its transition state. Specific boss meanings remain unresolved.

units.name: AdvanceEnemyAnimationOnEdge
units.summary: Call a movement-state edge detector and advance a two-state animation only when carry signals a completed active-to-idle transition. Continue to the ordinary object loop. Related controller entries use independently bounded animation cycles.

units.name: DetectEnemyStateEdge
units.summary: Return carry once after the primary object state becomes zero following a nonzero state. Store a one-bit latch in $6C; otherwise clear carry. The entry prefix jumps to the object loop.

units.name: DispatchRoomControllerState
units.summary: Dispatch the room completion state through seven inline words. Its timed handlers hide the controller, wait for contact and prepare the encoded password scene.

units.name: InitializeAltarPuzzle
units.summary: Load altar display/palette, initialize the actor and puzzle cursor, then update input/OAM each frame. $AE selects one of eight altar positions and $BA counts jewels placed. Nearby display words are inline pointers the actor helper records the selected jewel order.

units.name: AltarPuzzleInput
units.summary: Right/Left edges move the selected altar position within 0..7 and mark the actor moving. A places a jewel only when the actor has stopped. The helper selects the jewel pose, stores its order byte and advances the eight-jewel count.

units.name: ValidateJewelOrder
units.summary: Compare all eight placed-jewel bytes at $05F0 against the fixed sequence at mapped $A91E, descending from index 7. Any mismatch takes the failure wait; all equal takes the success wait. Local artificial probes reached success, not ending/credits.

units.name: WaitAfterWrongJewelOrder
units.summary: Load A=$3C and enter the frame wait at its STA handshake instruction ($F85A). This waits for 60 interrupt decrements, then advances frame phase once and retries the puzzle.

units.name: WaitAfterCorrectJewelOrder
units.summary: The matching-order branch waits for 60 interrupt decrements through the interior frame-wait entry, then enters the final scene setup. Natural boss defeat and natural ending entry remain separate from this supported continuation.

units.name: DrawNextAltarJewel
units.summary: Use placed-jewel count to choose the next jewel frame/flags. Count eight hides its object; otherwise position slot $F0 at a fixed screen location.

units.name: MoveAltarActorToSlot
units.summary: When stopped, display the idle altar frame. Otherwise configure movement/animation and compare actor world X (including facing offset) with the selected slot coordinate. Continue moving until both axes match.

units.name: FinishAltarActorMovement
units.summary: Choose horizontal facing from the selected slot X, then move toward its Y. Animate according to movement bits; clear movement state when no displacement is needed.

units.name: InitializeAltarActor
units.summary: Copy the 32-byte actor template, derive 12.4-style position accumulators by shifting pixel coordinates left four, preserve its frame and clear phase/timers, then set moving state. The exact accumulator width is two bytes, with four fractional bits.

units.name: FlashSceneScroll
units.summary: Use random low bits to toggle bit 2 of each horizontal scroll byte, wait a frame and repeat for the scene countdown. The continuation changes audio/CHR, waits and selects the ending variant before displaying its text pages.

units.name: UpdateObjectSlots
units.summary: Walk slots $40..F0 in $10-byte steps, skipping hidden objects at Y >= $F2. Preserve the slot around each behavior call. The per-object entry ticks two immunity timers before dispatch; hidden objects do not run these updates.

units.name: UpdateSpecialObjectCategories
units.summary: The kind attribute at $8A00 distinguishes ordinary objects from special $D0/$C0 categories. Special animation phases can restore a saved kind; intermediate phases set immunity and move vertically or dispatch state. Missing byte spans prevent identifying the complete life cycle or item names.

units.name: SelectObjectBehavior
units.summary: Resolve a 32-byte behavior descriptor from object kind. Visible objects enter descriptor-driven updates; an offscreen object instead dispatches the descriptor byte at offset $0B. This does not classify the inline dispatch words in the following gap.

units.name: LoadObjectBehaviorParameters
units.summary: Descriptor bytes 1..3 supply movement/collision flags, animation base and animation shift. Byte 0 selects a state machine through an inline table; $1C is a banked CPU pointer into the current data bank.

units.name: ObjectBehaviorMachineA
units.summary: Dispatch the selected object state. Its classified active path performs a ground/fall step, tests relative player/falcon position, and if needed replaces facing bits while preserving low palette bits; otherwise it enters direction-based motion. The rest of this behavior uses auxiliary countdowns, animation phase and a recovery state.

units.name: ObjectBehaviorMachineB
units.summary: Descriptor-selected emission machine with five supported states: wait for activation, prepare emission fields, animate/spawn, repeat or finish emission count, and recover to state zero. Shared falling/proximity/facing helpers are understood; original enemy identity remains unknown.

units.name: ObjectBehaviorMachineC
units.summary: A third state machine shares gravity/proximity checks. Its classified tail chooses the displayed frame from base kind plus a descriptor-derived per-object frame delta. Delay, movement, impulse and recovery states form the subsequent cycle.

units.name: DispatchObjectMovementMode
units.summary: Dispatch low four behavior flag bits through inline words. The selector is established; only independently supported low-nibble modes 0..6 have selected target words.

units.name: MoveObjectUsingDescriptor
units.summary: Load speed pair at descriptor offset 4, apply facing-directed horizontal movement and common animation. Another entry loads proximity bounds at offsets 8/9 and chooses player or falcon reference from offset 10 before a vertical comparison.

units.name: MoveObjectAndAnimate
units.summary: Load descriptor speed pair 4/5, move according to object facing, and tail-call common animation. Shared helper names refer to mechanics, not a particular enemy species.

units.name: AdvanceObjectPathPhase
units.summary: Animate, apply descriptor speed pair 6/7 and facing-directed motion. When movement does not complete, obtain speed pair 4/5 and advance or reverse the per-object path phase according to facing, wrapping the forward phase at $A8. Path-table consumers follow.

units.name: DispatchObjectPathTables
units.summary: Preserve the path phase across two dispatches: table $A608 chooses one movement action, then table $A558 chooses another. Each bounded $A8-byte prefix produces commands 0..2 the selected handlers change motion or return. Exact game trajectory meaning remains unresolved.

units.name: ReturnFromObjectAction
units.summary: This selected path action returns immediately; the next physical entry dispatches a separate randomized motion state machine.

units.name: StepObjectFallPhase
units.summary: Use per-object auxiliary phase to step a fall-speed table. Initially probe ground and enter falling if unsupported. Later nonzero table steps select vertical speed and call the down helper; marker value four follows the landing branch. The contact completion clears the auxiliary cursor and returns carry set; incomplete/no contact returns clear.

units.name: CheckObjectProximity
units.summary: Load alternating descriptor bounds, then compare the object with player or active falcon on alternating frames. Return carry clear when outside the selected vertical category; otherwise continue to the horizontal relation test. No original AI intent is assumed.

units.name: LoadAlternatingObjectBounds
units.summary: Use frame parity to select descriptor offset $10 or $18, retain its pointer, and copy eight bytes into the object auxiliary record. This permits alternating player/falcon tests without reloading every bound separately. A second entry resets a direction scratch byte and branches on facing.

units.name: MoveObjectRight
units.summary: Add horizontal speed to the two-byte position accumulator, which has four fractional bits. Convert to pixel target and advance pixel X one step at a time, checking right-edge collision, support and tile-category flags as requested by behavior bits. Return carry clear if no pixel change is needed. At the world accumulator limit clamp the pixel coordinate; obstruction uses a separate resynchronization entry.

units.name: MoveObjectLeft
units.summary: Subtract horizontal speed and advance pixel X toward the converted target one pixel at a time. Optional behavior flags check left-edge obstruction, support and special tile categories. Underflow clamps X at zero. This mirrors rightward motion but uses subtraction and left-edge probes.

units.name: ResyncObjectHorizontalAccumulator
units.summary: After blocked horizontal movement, derive the fractional accumulator from integer world X shifted left four. Commit both accumulator bytes, then use the prior motion nibble to preserve or reflect facing; terminal boundary handling hides the object.

units.name: MoveObjectDown
units.summary: Add vertical speed to its accumulator, convert from four fractional bits, and step screen Y toward the target. Behavior bit 6 enables collision probing. Count pixel motion in the animation counter; reaching the lower accumulator boundary clamps screen Y at $E0. Paired tile samples at $68 or above choose the common collision result.

units.name: MoveObjectUp
units.summary: Subtract vertical speed from its accumulator and step screen Y upward toward the converted target. Optional upper-edge tile probes can stop movement; underflow clamps Y at zero. The helper tails reconstruct the fixed-point Y accumulator or hide on terminal bounds.

units.name: LoadDescriptorSpeeds
units.summary: Y selects a horizontal/vertical speed pair. Object kind $39 forces horizontal speed 8 and vertical zero. Otherwise difficulty byte $07F4 scales horizontal descriptor speed to 1x, 1.5x or 2x; vertical speed is copied directly. The scaling uses integer half speed.

units.name: AnimateObjectFromMotion
units.summary: If animation base is zero, return. Otherwise shift the per-object animation counter by the configured amount, mask to four phases, map through the animation phase table, and add to object base frame.

units.name: CompareObjectHorizontalCenters
units.summary: Compute object/reference centers using sprite width and half world coordinates, then compare horizontal separation against half the configured bound. Very small separations (<8 in this representation) are excluded. On a match return side category 1/2, facing bit in $5C and carry set; otherwise return zero/carry clear. The bound byte is halved in place.

units.name: CompareObjectVerticalCenters
units.summary: Compute sprite-height-adjusted vertical centers for current object and selected reference slot. Compare signed separation to the configured vertical bound. A hit returns category 4 or 8 and vertical relation in $5D with carry set; no hit returns zero/carry clear.

units.name: ResolveObjectDescriptor
units.summary: Index the object attribute byte by kind, multiply by 32, then add $9800 to form the descriptor CPU pointer at $1C/$1D. The descriptor bank is the effective mapped data bank, not an inferred physical address.

units.name: ProbeObjectLeftEdge
units.summary: Probe only at an aligned left tile edge; otherwise return two zero tile categories. Use frame width/height and world X to read top/bottom points one pixel left of the object, returning categories in $98/$99.

units.name: ProbeObjectRightEdge
units.summary: Probe only when right edge is at the final pixel of a 16-pixel tile. Read the two tile categories just right of the object at its upper/lower body points. Return zero categories between tile boundaries.

units.name: ProbeObjectTopEdge
units.summary: Probe only at aligned object Y. Read map categories one pixel above the object at left/right extents. Zero result between tile boundaries avoids redundant collision work.

units.name: ProbePlayerSupport
units.summary: A retained platform-contact sentinel returns support category $72 for both sample points; otherwise use the normal bottom-edge probe.

units.name: ProbeObjectBottomEdge
units.summary: At a tile-aligned bottom edge, read the two map cells one pixel below the body. Between boundaries return zero categories. Frame-indexed width/height establish the probe positions.

units.name: ReadCollisionMapCell
units.summary: Convert world X and screen Y-minus-$20 into a 32-column, 16-pixel-cell RAM index rooted at $0600. Return its category byte; category $77 is treated as empty zero for collision. This lookup addresses RAM, independent of the banked source map copied there. Large following gaps and $FF data remain structurally separate.

units.name: InitializeNewStage
units.summary: Invalidate the HUD type cache, request interrupt mode $08, reset scroll, clear nametables and transfer inline display content. The following words are pointer data skipped by the helper through its saved return-address adjustment.

units.name: ResetStageResources
units.summary: Clear item/weapon/control fields and eight room-event markers, set a starting resource value and copy 16 status bytes from the current data bank. Then enter the common room initializer.

units.name: InitializeRoom
units.summary: Clear transition/lock/recovery/controller fields and all held/edge input bytes. Derive room metadata, hide old sprites, initialize room objects, copy/render the room map, load palette and initialize object accumulators. Each resource helper has explicit bank selection where classified.

units.name: InitializeRoomSpecialState
units.summary: Update camera, apply special room resource/controller defaults for composite room $38, and set room controller identity for final-room layouts. Stage 7 uses a separate controller table; ordinary country room 7 uses the country index. This supports probing bosses but does not prove an encountered boss.

units.name: ChooseRoomMusic
units.summary: When not in attract mode, select music by country and whether the room is entrance, room 7, or intermediate. Intermediate rooms preserve the current track when it already matches. Store the request for interrupt-side processing.

units.name: DeriveRoomMetadata
units.summary: A small prefix requests mode $0F. The metadata entry combines the selected country base with room index, chooses low-bank parity for map data, obtains CHR selections, and chooses a four-bank animation sequence. These values are mapper selections, not physical execution views.

units.name: ClearNametables
units.summary: Disable vertical PPU increment in the cached control byte, reset the PPU latch and write 2048 zero bytes from $2000. Rendering must already be disabled by the caller handshake; this routine does not wait for vblank.

units.name: ResetObjectRecords
units.summary: Fill all 16 object slots with the repeated 16-byte default template from $A288. Object records occupy $0300..03FF; auxiliary records live separately at $0400.

units.name: HideAllSprites
units.summary: Write hidden Y=$F8 into all 64 OAM shadow entries and initialize two OAM allocation cursors to $30. Does not perform DMA itself.

units.name: SelectRoomObjectData
units.summary: Choose stage pair bank by country index shifted right one. When retaining player state, reset records starting at slot $10; otherwise reset from slot zero.

units.name: ResetRoomObjectSlots
units.summary: Repeat the default template over the selected object slots. Construct the room object-record pointer from room index and stage parity. Retained-player entry chooses the opposite screen edge from prior Y sign; fresh entry initializes the player from the first record.

units.name: LoadRoomObjects
units.summary: Load player record, then process up to seven more four-byte records until $FF or no free slot. Each record is kind, flags, X-in-16-pixel-units and Y. Slot allocation starts at $40 and skips records whose Y is not hidden.

units.name: InitializeFalconAfterRoomLoad
units.summary: Temporarily force player state zero while updating the falcon, then restore the state. This initializes the falcon relative to the loaded player without losing player movement state.

units.name: AllocateRoomObjectSlot
units.summary: Scan slots $40..F0 for hidden Y=$F8. Load the record into the first free slot and return carry clear; return carry set when all are occupied. The record pointer/index are supplied by the caller.

units.name: LoadObjectRecord
units.summary: Read kind, flags, scaled X and Y into a selected object slot. X is expanded from a one-byte 16-pixel coordinate to two-byte world X. Preserve the original four-byte record in $0500 plus slot/4. A second entry chooses an object data bank from room metadata.

units.name: InitializeRoomObjectParameters
units.summary: Derive room event base and visit visible object slots from $20 upward. Resolve each descriptor and initialize position/state. Difficulty scales auxiliary health at descriptor offset $0D to 1x, 2x or 4x; player slot is excluded.

units.name: InitializeObjectMotion
units.summary: Resolve descriptor, convert integer coordinates into two-byte accumulators with four fractional bits, preserve base/display frame, load health byte $0E, and reset age, saved kind and immunity. X supplies the $10-aligned object slot.

units.name: PreparePlayerOverlapScan
units.summary: Prepare player world position and inset dimensions from frame-specific width/height. A selected attack type also probes projectile slot $30 before the ordinary object scan. X controls whether facing-dependent hitbox adjustments are included.

units.name: ScanPlayerObjectOverlap
units.summary: Scan visible objects $40..F0. An overlapping kind $39 is saved as platform contact; ordinary overlap stores target slot and side category. Later matching objects overwrite ordinary target selection; this is not necessarily nearest-object selection.

units.name: ScanAttackObjectOverlap
units.summary: Y selects the attack origin. Prepare its dimensions, scan visible object slots and return the first overlap with target slot and carry set. Exhausting slots returns carry clear. Unlike the player scan, this path stops on its first match.

units.name: PrepareObjectOverlapBounds
units.summary: Read candidate position and frame bounds. When requested, extend/offset its horizontal hitbox with frame-specific facing adjustments. Pass two-byte world X and one-byte Y to the signed separation comparisons.

units.name: CompareObjectOverlapBounds
units.summary: Subtract two-byte X, normalize negative distance and compare against the appropriate side width. Then compare absolute Y separation against the appropriate height. Return carry set for overlap and X=0/1 for horizontal side; reject different distant pages with carry clear.

units.name: BuildOamShadow
units.summary: Hide dynamic OAM entries from byte $10 onward. Render visible player unless its immunity phase blinks it, using camera-relative X and object frame metadata. OAM is shadow RAM here; interrupt-side DMA transfers it later.

units.name: BuildOtherObjectSprites
units.summary: Start object OAM allocation at the saved rotating cursor. Iterate slots $10..F0, skip hidden or blinking actors and render each metasprite, then retain the resulting cursor to rotate priority on later frames.

units.name: RenderObjectMetasprite
units.summary: Resolve column-major tile stream, width and height from parallel frame tables in the current $8000 bank. Adjust origin for facing and camera, skip offscreen columns, omit tile zero and emit four-byte OAM entries with shared attributes. Facing reverses horizontal column direction; vertical tile order is preserved. On cursor wrap resume at the reserved start cursor so fixed HUD sprites are protected.

units.name: TransferInlineVramCommands
units.summary: Entry $F3BA reads an inline pointer from the caller; $F3BD accepts an existing pointer. Each record is PPU address high/low, count with vertical-increment flag in bit 7, then count tile bytes. A negative address-high byte terminates. Reset the PPU latch for each record and advance the CPU pointer by count plus three. Caller must have disabled rendering or provided a suitable PPU access window.

units.name: ReadInlinePointerAndSkip
units.summary: Use the stack return address to read two inline pointer bytes following the caller JSR and advance that return address by two. Stack offsets are relative to this nested helper call. Each supported call site has a separate two-byte inline pointer record. This stack contract does not imply a layout for arbitrary unrelated gaps.

units.name: SelectStageSelectorGraphics
units.summary: Select map/tile/palette pointers for the country-selection screen, then enter common banked screen drawing.

units.name: SelectAltarGraphics
units.summary: Select the altar map/tile/attribute pointers, then enter common screen drawing. Adjacent title and ending entries select their own three source pointers.

units.name: DrawPreparedScreen
units.summary: Save the current data-bank selection and temporarily use bank 10. Copy a prepared map into RAM, draw 15 rows of 32 metatiles, then restore the previous data-bank selection. Drawing uses the PPU directly and requires the caller display handshake.

units.name: LoadRoomCollisionMap
units.summary: Select country-pair bank, locate the room map by $1C0-byte stride, and copy it into RAM at $0600. Draw rows 3..14, then select the common metatile-definition bank. Row bounds are explicit; source bytes outside the copied map are not implied part of it.

units.name: SelectRoomMetatileDefinitions
units.summary: Room metadata selects a four-byte metatile-definition bank/pointer and one of two attribute tables. Clear the special-object marker before rendering the map.

units.name: DrawMetatileMap
units.summary: Enable vertical PPU increment. Walk 32 cells per row from the RAM collision map, expanding each into tiles and attribute bits. If a special attribute mask was captured, read back and retain the corresponding PPU attribute bits after rendering.

units.name: CopyCollisionMapToRam
units.summary: Copy one full page and a bounded second page from ($16) to $0600/$0700. The caller supplies second-page count in $B3. Restore pointer high bytes afterward so the source pointer remains at its original page.

units.name: DetectSpecialMapObject
units.summary: Metatile IDs >= $78 create a special object at the map position and retain its VRAM address. Convert cell coordinates to screen/world fields and mark that its attribute mask must be saved. The following tile drawing uses the same metatile ID; no original object names are inferred.

units.name: DetectRoomEventTile
units.summary: Metatile $77 creates a room-event object and records its nametable address; place its actor at the tile center. These map markers are later interpreted by room-event logic and are treated as empty for collision.

units.name: CaptureRoomEventAddress
units.summary: Metatiles $5C/$5E record a related nametable address two rows above the cell for staged tile animation. Other IDs proceed directly to ordinary metatile drawing.

units.name: DrawMetatileAndAttributes
units.summary: Compute PPU nametable position from map row/column tables. Fetch four pattern indices from a four-byte metatile record and write two adjacent vertical columns. Derive the attribute byte address and quadrant mask, read-modify-write its palette bits, and when requested retain that mask/address for later special-object handling. PPU reads include the required buffered dummy read.

units.name: SelectScreenPalette
units.summary: X indexes a 32-byte palette record rooted at mapped $A758. Form the pointer and enter the palette staging helper.

units.name: SelectRoomPalette
units.summary: Select the country-pair bank and derive the room palette pointer from room index and stage parity. Source palette selection is independent of CHR mapping.

units.name: StagePaletteForInterrupt
units.summary: Copy 32 palette bytes into $05D0, set pending upload type 2 and wait for a frame handshake so the interrupt performs the PPU upload.

units.name: PollControllers
units.summary: Latch both standard controllers and shift eight serial button bits. Merge the alternate serial bit into each held state, then compute newly pressed edges as held AND NOT previous-held. $08/$09 are edges; $0A/$0B retain full held states. Bit order after shifting: A=$80, B=$40, Select=$20, Start=$10, Up=$08, Down=$04, Left=$02, Right=$01.

units.name: DispatchInlineJumpTable
units.summary: A selects a two-byte target following the caller JSR. Pop the return address into a temporary pointer, read the selected word starting at return+1, then JMP through it. This tail dispatch consumes that call return; target RTS returns to the caller of the dispatching routine. Table length and valid selectors must be established per call site.

units.name: ExpandByteToSixteenUnits
units.summary: Entry $F7E0 clears the high result byte; interior entry $F7E6 preserves its supplied high byte. Shift the two-byte value left four, returning low in A and high in $99. Used for object positions and motion accumulators.

units.name: NextRandomByte
units.summary: If the four-byte shift-register state is zero, seed it through an out-of-line helper. Advance eight feedback steps using XOR taps from the first byte, rotate across the four bytes, and return the last byte. The seed helper saves held controller input with a $55/$AA/$FF signature in the remaining three bytes.

units.name: RequestInterruptMode
units.summary: Store A as mode flags, set the interrupt handshake to 2 and spin until the interrupt decrements it to zero. A selects tasks/display state; it is not a frame count.

units.name: WaitForFrame
units.summary: Set the handshake to 1, spin until the interrupt decrements it to zero, then increment frame phase. Interior entry $F85A starts with STA $0C: A supplies the handshake directly there. Thus A=$3C waits for 60 decrements, subject to interrupts and exact caller setup; it does not use a separate delay loop.

units.name: ResetScrollState
units.summary: Clear horizontal scroll and nametable bits for both display sections. Set both vertical scroll bytes to $EE; subsequent room/camera initialization may replace the lower-section state.

units.name: SelectMenuChrBanks
units.summary: Initialize six CHR mapper selections for stage-selection or menu graphics, using distinct four-bank sprite sequences, then write them to MMC3.

units.name: SelectAltarChrBanks
units.summary: Choose altar CHR mapping (including $32 as the second paired selection), then enter the common MMC3 CHR writer. The following ending mapping uses a separate bank set.

units.name: ApplyChrBankSelections
units.summary: Write MMC3 registers 0..5 using selector values $80..85 and cached CHR bank values. Bit 7 fixes CHR inversion in each selection. This changes PPU pattern backing; it does not select CPU PRG slots.

units.name: ApplyPrgBankSelections
units.summary: Write MMC3 PRG registers 6/7 from cached $47/$48 using $86/$87, keeping the fixed-bank mode. These are register values; effective physical banks for source interpretation remain in phase-1 execution views.

units.name: NmiEntry
units.summary: Save A/X/Y, temporarily disable rendering and decrement the main-thread handshake once per NMI. Pending PPU work is then dispatched by type. An entry at $FA01 is an interior instruction, not a second independent handler.

units.name: NmiUploadPalette
units.summary: With upload type 2, write all 32 staged palette bytes to PPU $3F00 using horizontal increment. Reset the address latch/palette address before continuing to display tasks.

units.name: NmiUploadTileCommands
units.summary: If a nonzero upload type remains, consume commands at $05B0: address high/low, flagged count and payload, terminated by a negative address-high byte. Bit 7 of count selects vertical increment. Advance the source pointer over each record; do not interpret these RAM commands as immutable ROM data.

units.name: NmiCheckDisplayEnable
units.summary: Mode bit 0 decides whether to restore display state or skip directly to later tasks. This is independent of the main-thread frame handshake.

units.name: NmiRestoreSingleScroll
units.summary: When mode bit 1 is clear, DMA OAM shadow page 2, restore upper scroll/control/mask, and proceed to optional graphics/audio tasks. The alternate mode implements a split screen.

units.name: NmiPrepareSplitDisplay
units.summary: Build sprite zero from cached position, DMA OAM, and temporarily select HUD CHR banks. If tile/palette work already occurred, skip additional HUD work to bound interrupt time.

units.name: NmiRoomTileEventSave
units.summary: Handle staged room-event phases before normal HUD work. Phase 1 reads four columns of six nametable bytes into $0570, including one initial buffered read per column. Save the patch so it can later be restored.

units.name: NmiRoomTileEventPatch
units.summary: Phase 2 clears a four-column region (six or ten rows depending on entrance room); later phase restores the saved six-byte columns and clears event state. PPU vertical increment is selected for these operations. The patch uses cached nametable coordinates, not a new map classification.

units.name: NmiUpdateWeaponIcon
units.summary: Track selected secondary-attack type, deferring type change while its projectile is visible. On change, draw a two-by-two HUD icon from four tiles in the type table and retain the last drawn type.

units.name: NmiAnimateStatusBars
units.summary: Rotate through four status channels by frame phase. Move displayed resource one unit toward actual resource, update coarse segment counts at 8-unit boundaries, then draw the partial segment tile at a channel-specific nametable address. The fourth channel grows in the opposite address direction.

units.name: NmiApplySplitScroll
units.summary: Restore upper-section scroll and mask, wait for sprite-zero hit to clear then set, burn a short alignment delay, and install lower gameplay scroll. Busy polling requires a valid sprite-zero scene; a broken scene can stall here. No full timing/hardware compatibility claim follows.

units.name: NmiDispatchOptionalTasks
units.summary: Mode bit 2 applies cached CHR selections, then mode bit 3 selects audio processing. Task flags are independent; skipping audio proceeds to interrupt restore.

units.name: NmiMapAudioBanks
units.summary: Temporarily place PRG selections 8 and 9 into the switchable slots for the audio engine. Fixed interrupt code remains resident while audio routines/data are banked.

units.name: NmiProcessMusicRequest
units.summary: A nonnegative music request differing from current music starts a new stream with index masked to five bits. Consume the request with $FF and skip the ordinary audio tick on that NMI.

units.name: NmiProcessSoundRequest
units.summary: If no music replacement occurred, a nonnegative sound request starts an effect with five-bit index. Consume it with $FF; an absent request advances existing streams instead.

units.name: NmiAdvanceAudioAndRestorePrg
units.summary: Call audio tick when no new sound/music request is pending. Restore cached PRG selections before returning, so main-thread data context survives temporary audio banking.

units.name: NmiReturn
units.summary: Clear pending PPU upload, restore Y/X/A and RTI. The stack discipline matches the three-register entry save.

units.name: NmiApplyChrSelections
units.summary: Interrupt-side copy of the six-register MMC3 CHR writer, using cached selections and the same inversion mode. No mapper IRQ scheduling is implemented here.

units.name: IrqReturn
units.summary: Disable maskable interrupts and immediately RTI. The following classified $FF data is separate; no active scanline IRQ behavior is inferred.

units.name: ResetPrefix
units.summary: Disable IRQs, clear decimal mode and initialize stack. Begin clearing zero page with X=0. The continuation waits for vblank, clears RAM, preserves valid warm-start data and establishes effective PRG slots [6,13,14,15] before entering title code.
